Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - 7 days of fever with alternating hot/cold episodes and night sweats.
  - Recent travel: Returned from Vietnam ~4 weeks ago; rural trekking/cycling through farmland and city visits; took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug name not recalled).
  - Occupational exposure: Nurse, working while symptomatic but feeling too fatigued to continue.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset ~7 days ago; persistent fevers; OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen provide partial, temporary relief.
  - Associated: Diffuse myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, reduced fluid intake, fatigue. No clear localizing source.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable):
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: Not reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: Not reported.
  - Drooling: Not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported; reports seasonal allergic rhinitis history only.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: Not reported.
  - Dyspnea: Not reported.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): Not reported.
  - Ear symptoms: Denies ear pain.
  - Neck symptoms: Denies neck stiffness; no neck pain/swelling reported.
  - Sore throat/cough/cold symptoms: Denies.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - No prior similar febrile episodes reported; no prior ED visits or injection therapies for this issue.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as “not documented”).
  - Allergies: Pollen (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.
  - Current meds: Paroxetine (Seroxat) — dose/route/frequency not documented. OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen at recommended doses; specifics not documented. Malaria prophylaxis during travel — daily regimen; exact drug(s) not documented.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Lives/companionship not discussed. Plans to attend in-person clinic today.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - None reported/observed in teleconsultation.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - None reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Not reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise write “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded (teleconsultation; in-person exam planned).
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected febrile illness post-travel; malaria needs urgent exclusion.
- Evidence summary: 1 week of fever with chills/night sweats, myalgias, nausea, poor intake; no respiratory/ENT/urinary localizing symptoms. Recent rural travel in Vietnam 4 weeks ago with imperfectly protective prophylaxis. Clinician plans malaria testing (thick and thin films) and inflammatory markers after in-person exam.
- DDx (from DDx tool, aligned with transcript):
  1) Malaria (high likelihood): Compatible travel, paroxysmal fevers, sweats, myalgias; onset several weeks after return fits; prophylaxis not fully protective.
  2) Enteric fever (medium): Prolonged fever with minimal localizing features after SE Asia travel; no GI localizing signs noted (opposing).
  3) Common viral syndrome (medium): Systemic symptoms without focal signs; healthcare exposure; lack of URI symptoms argues slightly against.
- No ENT-specific pathology identified at this time.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - In-person evaluation today at central clinic for exam.
  - Laboratory testing after exam: Thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers and general blood work (per clinician plan).
  - Alternative if clinic not feasible: Attend local emergency department (ED).
  - Off work until diagnosis clarified and clinically improved.
  - Administrative: Patient to call the provided number to be booked; clinician to document requested tests in the visit note to present at reception.
- Patient instructions:
  - Attend clinic today as arranged; bring travel details and malaria prophylaxis information if available.
  - Maintain hydration as tolerated; continue antipyretics per OTC labeling if needed until evaluated.
  - Avoid strenuous activity; do not return to work until cleared.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Seek urgent care/ED immediately for any of the following: worsening fever with rigors, confusion, severe headache or neck stiffness, jaundice or dark urine, persistent vomiting, bleeding/bruising, chest pain, shortness of breath, or new ENT airway symptoms (voice change, throat tightness/closing, difficulty swallowing, drooling, noisy breathing).
- Follow-up:
  - Same-day clinic assessment with labs; further management guided by results.
  - Consider ID/travel medicine referral based on findings. No ENT referral indicated presently.

  - Detailed GI symptoms (constipation/diarrhea, abdominal pain), exposure to freshwater/insect bites, and vaccination history for typhoid/hep A.
